response.sql:
WITH high_fees AS (
  SELECT f.orderslink, o.dealedge, f.feerate, f.rebrate
  FROM fees f
  JOIN orders o ON o.recordvault = f.orderslink
  WHERE f.feerate > 0.0009
),
grp AS (
  SELECT orderslink, dealedge,
         AVG(feerate - rebrate) AS avg_net_rate,
         COUNT(*) AS record_count
  FROM high_fees
  GROUP BY orderslink, dealedge
),
side_avg AS (
  SELECT dealedge, AVG(avg_net_rate) AS side_avg
  FROM grp
  GROUP BY dealedge
)
SELECT g.orderslink,
       g.dealedge AS side,
       g.avg_net_rate,
       g.record_count,
       g.avg_net_rate - s.side_avg AS diff_from_side_avg
FROM grp g
JOIN side_avg s ON s.dealedge = g.dealedge
WHERE g.avg_net_rate > s.side_avg
ORDER BY diff_from_side_avg DESC NULLS LAST
LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: "High-rate" means feerate strictly greater than 0.0009 (the request does not say whether the cutoff is inclusive).
record_count counts all joined high-rate fee records in each group, including records whose net rate is missing (the 'ignore missing values' rule applies only to the average).
orders.recordvault is unique, as the documentation states, so the join does not duplicate fee records.
Side averages are taken over groups with a non-null average net rate, and orders.dealedge is non-null, since NULL sides would not join to their side average.

alternatives.interpretation: record_count counts only records that have a computable net rate (feerate and rebrate both present), matching the records that feed the average.
